title: Reward Bands
subtitle: Reinforcing selected signal features
altText: Chalkboard-style clinical diagram illustrating reward bands within a neurofeedback closed loop.
learningObjectives: Explain reward bands without diagnostic overreach.
Distinguish measurement, mechanism and clinical outcome in reward bands.
Identify one safety or validity limitation relevant to reward bands.

sections.explainSimply: A reward band is a frequency range or feature the learner is encouraged to increase or stabilise.
sections.explainLikePsychologist: Band boundaries, location, reference and state must be specified. Conventional labels such as alpha or beta cover heterogeneous activity.
sections.advancedClinicalDetail: Training a band assumes the selected feature is measurable, learnable and relevant to the target outcome. These assumptions require separate evaluation.
sections.thinkOfItLike: A rehabilitation plan: define the target, dose, measurement and stopping rule before changing the exercise.
sections.whyPsychologistsCare: Psychologists need to understand reward bands to evaluate mechanism claims, informed consent, treatment fit and whether change transfers to real-world function.
sections.whenItGoesWrong: “More” is not always better; excessive activation may worsen symptoms.
sections.clinicalPearl: The trained metric is an intermediate target; the clinical endpoint is meaningful function.
sections.practicalExample: A clinician using reward bands predefines the target, checks raw signal and artifacts, monitors symptoms and function, and reviews whether change generalises beyond the feedback display.
sections.limitationsCautions: “More” is not always better; excessive activation may worsen symptoms. Evidence classification: protocol-specific; evidence varies.
